rules: NEVER touch /Applications/Ghoztty.app in any way — it is the user's primary terminal. Debug app only: zig-out/Ghoztty-Debug.app (bundle id com.dzearing.ghoztty.debug, socket ghostty-debug-<uid>.sock).
All bundle identifiers stay in com.dzearing.ghoztty.* — NEVER com.mitchellh.*.
NEVER run +new-remote-window unattended against a possibly-unreachable host: a failed dial pops a modal alert that wedges ALL CLI IPC. Loopback dials to an agent you just health-checked are OK.
Use /usr/bin/log (never bare `log` — zsh builtin shadows it).
A `kill -STOP`ed process gets pending teardown signals delivered at SIGCONT — run freeze/thaw cycles in one tool call.

Stale-instance trap: after rebuilding, verify the debug app process start time > binary mtime before trusting live behavior. Kill any debug instance launched from other/deleted worktrees first (the user's real terminal is the RELEASE app; killing DEBUG instances is safe unless this effort created live test windows).
Agent test seam: GHOSTTY_AGENT_LOCK=<path> GHOSTTY_AGENT_HEARTBEAT=<path> lets a test agent run beside any real one. Agent flag is --listen=127.0.0.1:<port> (there is no --port flag).

+split --name= on remote/agent-backed windows registers the pane ASYNCHRONOUSLY since T04 (onCreate callback after the cwd RPC; loopback ≈ ms, real remote = latency-bound) — poll briefly before using the name, or use +list to discover panes.
If the user interrupts with new instructions, encode them as tasks in this file instead of drifting.

NEVER 'tell process "ghoztty"' by NAME in System Events — the RELEASE app has the same process name and it WILL be targeted (this created a tab in the user's real terminal once). Scope by pid ('first process whose unix id is N') or better: use the app's own AppleScript interface via 'tell application id "com.dzearing.ghoztty.debug"'.

Driving tabs headlessly: the scripting interface (new tab / close tab / select tab / windows / tabs) works even while the SCREEN IS LOCKED; AX menu-bar clicks do NOT (zero AX windows exposed, action silently no-ops). 'new tab in (first window whose id is "tab-group-…")' — ids match +list. Known wart: 'new tab' errors -10000 even on success (T06d); re-discover the pane via +list.
Screen locked also means the KEYCHAIN is locked — relay-account loads can block for minutes (observed 185s, off-main).
Do not kill -9 + relaunch the app with <2s gap until T06b is fixed: the restore probe races the agent's dead-peer detection and DESTROYS manifest entries for live sessions.

decisions: Direction: design doc §5 hybrid — local ghoztty-agent owns PTYs; viewer keeps a layout+sessionId manifest; agent later gains disk metadata for reboot floor. User approved 2026-07-13 ('let's try it').
v0 local transport = loopback TCP (both ends already exist: agent --listen, ghostty_remote_connection_new_tcp). Unix-socket + peercred is a hardening task AFTER the headline E2E works (T09).
session-persistence is an opt-in config flag initially (default off) so the debug app stays usable throughout.
Ring stays 2 MB default for the demo; configurable size + 16 MB default comes with T11.
Reboot recovery (agent disk persistence, RELAUNCH) comes after the upgrade demo (T12/T13) — the upgrade scenario keeps the agent alive, so it does not need disk persistence.

tasks.notes:
2026-07-15: done. APPROACH = wire shape (a): a new additive OPEN field `argv: ?[]const []const u8` the agent execs VERBATIM in place of its `<shell> -lic/-li` synthesis. Chose client-side (a) over agent-side (b) — same reasoning as T04b (reuse the existing OPEN wire, ZERO agent/protocol logic beyond one field, keep the lean agent binary free of shell_integration.zig + resources-dir lookup). The client already had integration.command from shell_integration.setup() (T04b); T04c just splits it into an argv array and forwards it.

WIRING (4 layers): (1) src/remote/protocol.zig Open gains `argv: ?[]const []const u8 = null` (additive; `emit_null_optional_fields=false` elides it, `ignore_unknown_fields=true` → older agents ignore it and keep `-li`). (2) src/termio/Remote.zig: Config.argv + backend field, duped element-by-element into the backend arena in init, set in the OPEN built by threadEnter. (3) src/Surface.zig appendLocalShellIntegrationEnv: return type void→`!?[]const []const u8`. For zsh/fish/elvish it returns null (their integration is env-only; forwarding argv would STRIP the `-li` login/interactive flags — the agent default is exactly right for them). tasks.notes: 2026-07-15: done. ROOT CAUSE was NOT agent-side (the ATTACH gap-fill at server.zig:784-816 was correct) — it was a CLIENT-side registration RACE. The client uses TWO separate reader threads over TWO independent streams (connection.zig: control_thread + data_thread, `control`/`data` Streams). On ATTACH the agent frames ATTACHED on the CONTROL lane and the whole ring replay as DATA on the DATA lane. The client only calls channels.register(ch) AFTER the control-lane ATTACHED reply unblocks the caller (connection.zig:1597, attachChannelCancellable). Because the two lanes have NO cross-stream ordering, the data thread frequently ran routeInboundData for the replay DATA BEFORE register() completed → ChannelTable.pushTo found no channel → returned .unknown → bytes DROPPED (inbound_ring.zig old line 388). Microsecond race → per-pane coin-flip, exactly the 'same agent, same cycle, different panes' symptom. Fresh OPEN-new rarely bit because a new shell emits no output for ~ms; ATTACH replay dumps the ring instantly. FIX (client-only, additive): ChannelTable gained a bounded pre-registration buffer `pending: map<channel, ArrayList(u8)>`. pushTo now BUFFERS bytes for a not-yet-registered channel (new RouteResult variant `.buffered`) instead of dropping; register() FLUSHES pending[ch.id] into the ring under the SAME mutex right after map.put, so buffered (pre-register) bytes always precede live (post-register) bytes and none are lost — atomic vs. concurrent pushTo. Bounds: max_pending_bytes_per_channel=256KiB (one client ring), max_pending_channels=16 (hostile-input cap); over-cap excess dropped (old behavior); deregister/deinit free un-claimed buffers. connection.zig routeInboundData treats `.buffered` like `.unknown` (no FLOW). Since real ATTACH always sends last_byte_offset=0 (Remote.zig:264, resync_active=false), no resync-trim interaction; test_client resync path pre-registers so never buffers. This ALSO closes the same latent race for OPEN-new. COMMIT: 4337a9c23. steps: Build a second copy of the bundle (or rebuild after touching a version string); rsync --delete over zig-out staged copy in a scratch dir — NEVER /Applications.
Also test the graceful path: normal quit (isQuitting) instead of SIGKILL, then swap+relaunch — both must pass.
Verify the agent process was untouched across the swap (same agent PID before/after).
Record results (timings, any scrollback truncation) in this file's notes and the design doc's acceptance table.
tasks.acceptance: Upgrade-mode script passes 3 consecutive runs for BOTH kill -9 and graceful-quit variants; agent PID unchanged; report written.
tasks.notes:
2026-07-15: done, commit ea76e4a19. Extended scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py with --upgrade + --quit=kill|graceful (no app-source changes). UPGRADE = between terminate and relaunch, PHYSICALLY REPLACE the installed bundle on disk: rm -rf + fresh copy from a pristine byte-identical reserve, so every file gets a new inode at the SAME installed zig-out path (asserted: main-exec inode changes each cycle) — exactly the FS swap Sparkle does — then relaunch from it. BOTH quit modes 3/3 PASS, agent PID unchanged across every swap. Recovery gap (old-process-gone -> all panes interactive): kill ~3-8s, graceful ~3s; measured SEPARATELY from termination time (the <10s SLA is recovery speed, not quit speed). Results table added to design doc §2; README §--upgrade documents the flags + rationale.

HARD-WON DESIGN CALL (why byte-identical, NOT a recompiled/re-signed binary): my first cut bumped CFBundleVersion + `codesign --force --sign -` each cycle to get a provably-different Mach-O. That SPAMMED a keychain password prompt ('Ghoztty[DEBUG] wants to use com.dzearing.ghoztty.relay-account') on EVERY launch — the user hit this live and stopped me. ROOT CAUSE: the debug bundle is AD-HOC signed (TeamIdentifier not set); the login-keychain ACL for the relay-account item is a trusted-application entry keyed by the app's exact cdhash (its designated requirement is `cdhash H"..."`). Re-signing mints a NEW cdhash not in the ACL -> prompt; a plain launch of the already-authorized zig-out cdhash (4d477ee3...) is silent (that's why T07 never prompted). Under ad-hoc signing there is NO way to change the binary silently — a real Sparkle upgrade is Developer-ID signed with a STABLE DR across versions, so it doesn't prompt; we can't replicate that. FIX: the swap keeps content byte-identical (same cdhash -> zero prompts), verified by comparing reserve vs installed cdhash before the run. This is immaterial to the AC: the restore path never reads app-bundle bytes (it reads the layout manifest + the surviving agent); the full FS-swap->relaunch->re-attach path IS exercised, and the app relaunches from a physically-replaced-on-disk bundle. The app ALWAYS launches from the installed zig-out path (never a /tmp copy) to guarantee the authorized cdhash. Teardown restores zig-out from the reserve if a crash ever interrupts a swap.

DISCOVERED A REAL PRE-EXISTING BUG -> T08a: a GRACEFUL quit (Cmd-Q / AppleScript) of a session-persistence app with several agent-backed panes HANGS ~45s in AppKit window teardown before exiting (plain exec-backed 5-pane app quits in 0.6s — proven session-persistence-specific). 45s sample: main thread spins a nested run loop inside -[NSApplication _terminateFromSender:askIfShouldTerminate:saveWindows:] (582/593 samples idle in CFRunLoop mach_msg), waking to run _deallocHardCore: -> -[NSWindow _closeForTermination] -> TerminalWindow.close() -> tab-group cleanup that RE-ENTERS TransparentTitlebarTerminalWindow.setupTabGroupObservation()/NSWindowStackController addWindow: (rebuilding tab-bar UI + SwiftUI ViewGraph DURING window close). Agent connection threads are just idle-reading (not the cause). applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateNow FAST and the isQuitting/flushPendingSyncs manifest path runs BEFORE the hang, so persistence + recovery are unaffected; the harness waits the hang out (graceful_quit timeout 45s) then SIGKILLs as last resort. Left the box CLEAN (teardown resets everything incl. staging; zig-out valid + byte-identical). T04a is now unblocked.

tasks.title: Graceful quit hangs ~45s with multiple agent-backed panes
tasks.goal: SEEN LIVE (T08): Cmd-Q / AppleScript 'quit' of a session-persistence app with several agent-backed (.remote) panes wedges ~45s in AppKit window teardown before the process exits; a plain exec-backed 5-pane app quits in 0.6s, so it is session-persistence-specific and scales with pane/window count. Persistence is NOT affected (applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateNow fast; the isQuitting/flushPendingSyncs manifest path runs before the hang; recovery after relaunch is <4s) — but a user quitting the app hangs for ~45s, which is unacceptable UX and forces the E2E harness to SIGKILL as a fallback.
steps: Reproduce with scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py --quit=graceful (any --cycles); or build the 5-pane scenario and `osascript -e 'tell application id "com.dzearing.ghoztty.debug" to quit'`, then `sample <pid> 45`.

Sample evidence (T08): main thread spins a nested run loop in -[NSApplication _terminateFromSender:askIfShouldTerminate:saveWindows:] (582/593 samples idle in CFRunLoop __CFRunLoopServiceMachPort/mach_msg), waking to run -[NSApplication _deallocHardCore:] -> -[NSWindow _closeForTermination] -> @objc TerminalWindow.close() (TerminalWindow.swift:268) -> _finishClosingWindow -> _doTabbedWindowCleanupForOrderOut -> NSWindowStackController removeWindow:/addWindow: which RE-ENTERS TransparentTitlebarTerminalWindow.setupTabGroupObservation() (TransparentTitlebarTerminalWindow.swift:146/163) -> syncAppearance -> KVO, rebuilding NSTabBar items + SwiftUI ViewGraph DURING termination. Agent connection threads (client_mux.pumpThreadMain read, connection.writerLoop condition wait) are idle — NOT the cause.

Hypotheses to test: (a) terminate: is spinning the run loop waiting on an async per-window teardown that only completes for agent-backed surfaces (does closing a .remote surface post async work that never signals during termination?); (b) a tab-group KVO re-entrancy: closing one window mutates the shared tab group, firing setupTabGroupObservation which re-adds to the stack controller, snowballing with window count; (c) interaction with the T06 disableAppKitRestorationForSessionLayout / willEncodeRestorableState gating during saveWindows:.

Likely fix area: TerminalWindow.close()/TransparentTitlebarTerminalWindow tab-group observation teardown, or making agent-backed surface close synchronous/bounded at termination. Add a regression check (graceful quit of N agent-backed panes completes < ~3s) — the harness already measures term=…s.
tasks.acceptance: Graceful quit (Cmd-Q) of a session-persistence app with >=5 agent-backed panes exits in < ~3s (no SIGKILL fallback needed); E2E --quit=graceful reports term < 5s; persistence/recovery still pass.
tasks.notes:
2026-07-15: done — MISDIAGNOSIS. There is NO app-side graceful-quit hang. The '~45s hang' was a TEST-HARNESS ZOMBIE-REAPING ARTIFACT, and the original T08 `sample` that pointed at _terminateFromSender/setupTabGroupObservation was a sample of the ALREADY-EXITED (zombie) process showing its frozen exit-path stack. Fix is harness-only (scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py); ZERO src/ or macos/ changes.

HOW I PROVED IT (per CLAUDE.md 'reproduce first'): reproduced the 45s via the harness (--quit=graceful reliably term=49.2s), then instrumented the app termination timeline with timestamped os_log/NSLog at applicationShouldTerminate, applicationWillTerminate (+before/after ipcServer.stop), windowWillClose, TerminalWindow.close, BaseTerminalController.deinit, ghostty_surface_free (Swift Task.detached), the Zig io_thread stop+join, AND a self-registered atexit handler. Timeline showed EVERYTHING completes in ~7ms: shouldTerminate→willTerminate→ipcServer.stop→all TerminalWindow.close→io_thread join DONE→atexit FIRED, all within milliseconds of the quit. The process then sat until the harness SIGKILLed it at 45s. `sample` couldn't attach (needs sudo; password-gated), so I inspected via a minimal Python repro that launches the app EXACTLY like the harness (subprocess.Popen, start_new_session, Popen handle discarded/unreaped) and, after an AppleScript quit, polled BOTH os.kill(pid,0) and `ps -o stat=`: within 0.6s ps_stat went Ss→Z (ZOMBIE) and STAYED Z for 30s+, while os.kill(pid,0) returned True the ENTIRE time; os.waitpid(pid,WNOHANG) then reaped it as (pid, 0) — conclusive. atexit fired in ms in that repro too.

ROOT CAUSE: the app exits cleanly and fast, but as a child of the Python harness it becomes a ZOMBIE (defunct) until reaped. The harness's pid_alive() used os.kill(pid,0), which reports a zombie as ALIVE until its parent waitpid()s it. graceful_quit() waits the full 45s for the pid to 'disappear', never reaps → times out → SIGKILL (no-op on a zombie) → 'hang'. (The kill -9 path never showed this because it caps wait_gone at a fixed 5s and ignores the result; graceful waited 45.) Neither pane count nor tab groups mattered — a zombie doesn't 'scale'; the earlier 'scales with pane/window count' was noise. The 'exec quits in 0.6s' comparison in T08 was measuring the true exit, not this harness's wait_gone.

FIX (scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py, harness-only): (1) pid_alive() rewritten to be zombie-aware — reap our own launched children first, then consult `ps -o state= -p PID` and treat a zombie (state starts 'Z') or a missing pid as NOT alive (a zombie has already run exit() → for 'has the app finished terminating?' it IS gone). (2) launch_app() now retains every Popen in a module list `_launched_procs`; new `_reap_children()` polls them (Popen.poll() reaps finished children) so a cleanly-exited app turns from zombie to truly-gone. (3) graceful_quit timeout 45→20s (now just a safety net; real exit is <1s) and corrected the misleading T08a comments in graceful_quit + the recovery-gap block.

VERIFIED (clean rebuild, all instrumentation reverted via git checkout, byte-identical-cdhash concern N/A since no bundle bytes changed by intent — normal rebuild): --quit=graceful --cycles=3 = 3/3 PASS with term=0.2s each, NO SIGKILL fallback (was 49.2s+SIGKILL). Regressions clean: --quit=kill --cycles=2 = 2/2 PASS; --upgrade --quit=graceful --cycles=1 = PASS term=0.2s, bundle swapped, agent untouched. No leftover zombie/app processes after runs (box left clean by teardown). No src/ or macos/ changes ⇒ test-agent/app build unaffected (app still builds). COMMIT: 0ad0b2e29.
